newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan port seeks new proposal for LPG terminal.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan port seeks new proposal for LPG terminal.

text.p: Pakistan's state Port Qasim Authority (PQA) on Thursday invited new proposals by August 16 from private firms for the construction of a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) terminal and storage facilities.
Last June, the PQA had scrapped an earlier tender for construction of the LPG terminal without giving any reasons.

Port Qasim, Karachi's second port, said in a statement the terminal was being offered on build, operate and transfer basis with a concession period of 30 years but added that the concession would be on non-exclusive basis and there would be no throughput guarantees.
It said the terminal should be capable of handling tankers in the range of 4,000 to 5,000 dead weight tonnes (DWT) with an annual throughput capacity of 500,000 tonnes.

The essential components of the terminal should include a new jetty with mooring facilities to exclusively handle LPG tankers, approach or pipe trestle, marine loading arms, cargo heaters, pumps, pipelines, fire-fighter equipment and ancillary buildings, it said.

The PQA swill provide infrastructure at the terminal's periphery with cost to be charged to the terminal operator, the statement said. However, it parties who had submitted proposal in response to the earlier invitation "need not apply afresh".

Several foreign oil firms including U.S.-based Mobil Corp and the Royal Dutch Shell Group had submitted their proposals to build the terminal, likely to cost more than $20 million, in collaboration with Pakistani firms.
